items.title: George "Pops" Foster and Mugsy Spanier Interview, 1957-04-21
items.q: After Ted Lewis I couldn't stand it any longer. I went with Benny Pollack.

ctx.x: That's what I'm getting outside, man. I'll show you. I'll show you. Look over there. And my main scribe was trying to get in the town and stay there while trying to give me a place where Lally's got a nice house and shit. I don't care if she had a husband. I don't even care. Even that landlady, you get a free rent to clothes wash. She's a fool. I got to throw her in many places, too, man. Well, we go from here now.

When you were first started, were you studying music? Or who did you start thinking? No, I started out thinking first, then I started to study. Later? Oh, yeah. After I was playing professionally about two years, then I started to study. Because you couldn't play in bands. You couldn't go to a pit or anything with that if you couldn't read. Well, from Ray Miller, yeah, I went to Ted Lewis. That was a nice sentence. Eight years hardly. How many years? Eight years. Eight years. I don't know what a depression was. I…

What hospital did you go to New Orleans, to Turo? That's where you are. You remember Turo Infirmary? Yeah. That's where every night when you called your number I said Turo Infirmary. But I didn't know that was the hospital you see here. See, I didn't know you knew what I was talking about. I said sure. Are you calling you all wrong?
